protections: Recognized password, hidden, sensitive-autocomplete, disabled, readonly, invisible, ambiguous-identity, framed, shadow-root, and opted-out fields are denied before value capture or transport
Context is capped independently at 512 Unicode scalars before and 128 after the selection and rejects ill-formed UTF-16 before transport
Native hello negotiation, extension sender, exact fixture URL, frame, document lifecycle, and immutable session route are validated
The extension requests only nativeMessaging API permission and broadcasts its shortcut state only to frozen deduplicated routes that were previously bound from trusted content senders
Post-display field, ancestor, identity, constraint, document-visibility, DOM-lifecycle, and native-transport invalidation cancel pending work and clear the controller before later insertion
Non-global actions bind session, focus epoch, revision, fingerprint, and suggestion ID
Encoded broker frames are rejected above 65536 bytes before body allocation
Suggestion output is capped at 64 Unicode scalars and eight words and rejects controls, format characters, line separators, and unpaired surrogates
Latest-wins cancellation, receiver-local TTL expiry, addressed broker clears, and a single-use bounded commit lease fail closed
Normal broker errors and health output are content-free; health redacts locator tokens
exclusions: Live Chromium extension lifecycle, native-host framing, profile installation, and browser layout
Arbitrary origins, file or restricted schemes, incognito, iframes, and broad web compatibility
Search, URL, telephone, email, password, hidden, and every other non-text input type
contenteditable, shadow DOM, framework-controlled fields, anonymous or duplicate identities, and selection replacement
Verified native undo, framework state, trusted input events, or absence of autosave, validation, search, network, and application side effects
Persisted origin policy, policy epochs, and a cross-connection pause broadcast-ack or commit-revocation barrier
Routing unsolicited omatypectl request or acceptance output into a Chromium content controller
Obsidian, Firefox, Fcitx5, IBus, terminal, semantic-model, remote-provider, personalization, and production compatibility claims
notes: No extension, native host, browser profile, desktop configuration, local model, or service was installed by this foundation

The public development manifest key freezes extension ID ckkiehcjbclcjckkkajohopoikeejkoa; the static content match and both content/service-worker runtime gates require exactly http://localhost:4173/chromium.html
The target page remains hostile and can observe or remove the ghost host, alter the field during event dispatch, intercept the input event, or trigger application and network side effects
An exact typed-through remainder is display-only until a fresh provider response binds it to the new revision and fingerprint
Partial word acceptance clears the old remainder and schedules a new addressed request before another acceptance

A browser-shortcut pause clears reachable controllers, but an external CLI pause can leave controllers locally unnotified; their repeated requests are rejected before provider work or new commit authorization
The M1 broker cannot prove that a commit.prepare already transmitted on another connection cannot mutate after pause acknowledgement
omatypectl request and acceptance commands exercise broker-core behavior only in M1 and do not control a Chromium page
Same-UID native-broker impersonation and unmarked secrets in ordinary text fields remain inside the declared trusted-local-component and residual-risk boundary
Omatype is an internal codename with a known public collision; public naming, technical namespaces, and source licensing remain release gates
